title: Jim Weatherall: OU's First Outland Trophy Winner in 1951
question: Who was the first Oklahoma Sooner to win the Outland Trophy?
answer: Tackle Jim Weatherall was the first Oklahoma player to win the Outland Trophy, taking the award as the nation's top interior lineman in 1951. He was a consensus All-American in 1950 and a unanimous All-American in 1951.
summary: Jim Weatherall became the first Sooner to win the Outland Trophy in 1951. Learn how the two-time All-America tackle and kicker anchored Bud Wilkinson's OU.
body: Long before Oklahoma piled up a trophy case full of national hardware, a big tackle named Jim Weatherall opened the door. In 1951 he became the first Sooner ever to win the Outland Trophy, the Football Writers Association of America's award for the best interior lineman in college football.

Weatherall was built for the job. The National Football Foundation lists him at 6-foot-4 and 230 pounds, a four-year letterman who wore No. 71 and served as a co-captain in 1951. He was a consensus All-American in 1950 and a unanimous pick in 1951, and he earned all-conference honors twice. OU's own history notes that he cleared the way for an offense that ranked ninth nationally in rushing and seventh in total offense.

He was also a weapon with his foot. Weatherall handled place-kicking for the Sooners, booting 37 extra points in 1950, fifth-best in the nation, and 39 more in 1951, second-best nationally. During his time in Norman, Oklahoma went 39-4, put together a 31-game winning streak and claimed the 1950 national championship.

Off the field he was a Naval ROTC member who earned a business administration degree, then served in the Marines. The Philadelphia Eagles drafted him in the second round in 1952, and the NFF credits him with a nine-season pro career from 1954 to 1962 that included stops in Edmonton, Philadelphia, Washington and Detroit.

Weatherall was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1992, the same year he passed away. Every Sooner lineman who has since claimed the Outland, from J.D. Roberts to Jammal Brown, followed the trail he blazed.
